structure.title: Proper motion, spectra, and timing of PSR J1813−-1749 usingChandraandNICER
structure.abstract:
AbstractPSR J1813−-1749 is one of the most energetic rotation-powered pulsars known,
producing a pulsar wind nebula (PWN) and gamma-ray and TeV emission,
but whose spin period is only measurable in X-ray.
We present analysis of twoChandradatasets that are separated by
more than ten years and recentNICERdata.
The long baseline of theChandradata allows us to derive a pulsar
proper motionμR.A.=−(″​067±″​010)​yr-1\mu_{\rm R.A.}=-(0.\!\!″067\pm 0.\!\!″010)\mbox{ yr${}^{-1}$}andμdecl.=−(″​014±″​007)​yr-1\mu_{\rm decl.}=-(0.\!\!″014\pm 0.\!\!″007)\mbox{ yr${}^{-1}$}and velocityv⟂≈900−1600​km s-1v_{\perp}\approx 900-1600\mbox{ km s${}^{-1}$}(assuming a distanced=3−5d=3-5kpc),
although we cannot exclude a contribution to the change in measured
pulsar position due to a change in brightness structure of the PWN
very near the pulsar.
We model the PWN and pulsar spectra using an absorbed power law
and obtain best-fit absorptionNH=(13.1±0.9)×1022​cm-2N_{\rm H}=(13.1\pm 0.9)\times 10^{22}\mbox{ cm${}^{-2}$}, photon indexΓ=1.5±0.1\Gamma=1.5\pm 0.1, and 0.3–10 keV luminosityLX≈5.4×1034​erg s-1​(d/5 kpc)2L_{\rm X}\approx 5.4\times 10^{34}\mbox{ erg s${}^{-1}$}(d/\mbox{ 5 kpc})^{2}for the PWN andΓ=1.2±0.1\Gamma=1.2\pm 0.1andLX≈9.3×1033​erg s-1​(d/5 kpc)2L_{\rm X}\approx 9.3\times 10^{33}\mbox{ erg s${}^{-1}$}(d/\mbox{ 5 kpc})^{2}for PSR J1813−-1749.
These values do not change between the 2006 and 2016 observations.
We useNICERobservations from 2019 to obtain a timing model of PSR J1813−-1749,
with spin frequencyν=22.35​Hz\nu=22.35\mbox{ Hz}and spin frequency
time derivativeν˙=(−6.428±0.003)×10−11​Hz s-1\dot{\nu}=(-6.428\pm 0.003)\times 10^{-11}\mbox{ Hz s${}^{-1}$}.
We also fitν\numeasurements from 2009–2012 and our 2019 value
and find a long-term spin-down rateν˙=(−6.3445±0.0004)×10−11​Hz s-1\dot{\nu}=(-6.3445\pm 0.0004)\times 10^{-11}\mbox{ Hz s${}^{-1}$}.
We speculate that the difference in spin-down rates is due
to glitch activity or emission mode switching.
